sensitive_conditions: The norm and Taylor regularization coefficient must match the statement.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic bound for every completed admissible k-step execution.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The entire displayed dependence on p is c_p. No additional dimension factor is asserted.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact pth-order Taylor polynomial at trial base points and exact gradients at accepted output points. No noisy or inexact oracle transfer is asserted.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Last accepted point yk; scalar value gap f(yk)-min f.
complexity_scope.regime: Integer p>=2, d>=1, k>=1, Lp>0; unconstrained convex minimization with an attained minimum.
complexity_scope.resource: k accepted outer iterations only. Line-search trials, accepted-point gradient queries, and model-solution arithmetic are separate resources, not bounded by this extracted statement.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Selected exact accepted execution of ATD Algorithm 1, whose recurrence and acceptance conditions are fully specified in this statement. No coverage of arbitrary algorithms and no lower bound is asserted.

proofs.locator: PDF pp.3–5, Theorem 2.1 and Lemmas 2.2–2.6; p.6, Lemma 3.1; pp.7–8, Section 3.3 and Lemmas 3.3–3.4
map: PDF pp.3–4, Lemmas 2.2–2.4: define psi0(x)=||x||^2/2 and psii=psi_{i-1}+ai f1(x,yi). Convexity bounds psii above by Ai f(x)+||x||^2/2; xi minimizes psii. The induction inequality prepares the potential comparison.

PDF p.5, Lemma 2.5: lambda_i Ai=ai^2 and the approximate implicit-gradient residual give psi_k(xk)-Ak f(yk)>=(1-sigma^2)/2 sum_i (Ai/lambda_i)||yi-xtilde_{i-1}||^2. With Lemmas 2.2–2.3 this yields f(yk)-f(x*)<=||x*||^2/(2Ak) and the weighted displacement bound (6). Lemma 2.6 supplies sqrt(Ak)>=sum_i sqrt(lambda_i)/2.

PDF p.6, Lemma 3.1: exact Taylor-model optimality, gradient Taylor remainder bounded by Lp||y-xtilde||^p/p!, and acceptance eta in [1/2,p/(p+1)] imply residual at most half the displacement. Thus sigma=1/2 is applicable to the Section 2 potential.

PDF p.7, Lemma 3.3 equations (15)–(16): acceptance and the weighted displacement bound give sum_i Ai/lambda_i^((p+1)/(p-1))<=Cp||x*||^2, where Cp=8(Lp/(p-1)!)^(2/(p-1)). Reverse Hölder with q=(3p+1)/(2(p+1)) and Lemma 2.6 convert this to an accumulated-weight inequality.

PDF p.8, Lemma 3.4 and conclusion of Section 3.3: apply the sequence-growth lemma to Bk=Ak^((p-1)/(3p+1)) with alpha=(p+1)/(p-1), obtaining the stated lower bound Ak>=k^((3p+1)/2)/(c_p Lp||x*||^(p-1)). Section 3.3 combines this with the potential gap estimate to establish equation (1). The displayed Theorem 1.1 bound is retained; no sharper constant or reconstructed local theorem is submitted.
proofs.omitted_details: This is a faithful literature proof map, not an independent reproof. The source's internal lemmas remain source-local dependencies rather than invented scientific IDs. Section 4 is unnecessary for the conditional outer-iteration statement and its oracle implementation theorem is not asserted here.
proofs.reading_coverage: Read the relevant statements and proof text on PDF pp.3–8 and visually inspected those original-page derivatives. Theorem 1.1 and Algorithm 1 on pp.1–2 were also visually inspected.

assumptions: f:R^d->R is convex and C^p; for every u,v in R^d, ||D^p f(u)-D^p f(v)||op<=Lp||u-v||.
A minimizer x* in argmin f exists.
Every one of the k accepted updates satisfies 1/2<=lambda_{i+1}Lp||y_{i+1}-xtilde_i||^(p-1)/(p-1)!<=p/(p+1), with exact model minimization and exact gradient updates as defined above.
statement.conclusion: f(yk)-f(x*)<=c_p Lp||x*||^(p+1)/k^((3p+1)/2). This is equation (1) of Theorem 1.1 in the selected p>=2 regime. The separate oracle-call assertion in Theorem 1.1 is not part of this extracted outer-iteration conclusion.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use Euclidean norm on R^d and its induced multilinear operator norm. Define f_p(w,z)=f(z)+sum_{j=1}^p D^j f(z)[w-z]^j/j! and c_p=2^(p-1)(p+1)^((3p+1)/2)/(p-1)!. For a sequence define A0=0, x0=y0=0. At each i=0,...,k-1 let lambda_{i+1}>0, a_{i+1}=(lambda_{i+1}+sqrt(lambda_{i+1}^2+4lambda_{i+1}Ai))/2, A_{i+1}=Ai+a_{i+1}, and xtilde_i=(Ai yi+a_{i+1}xi)/A_{i+1}. Require y_{i+1}=argmin_w {f_p(w,xtilde_i)+(Lp/p!)||w-xtilde_i||^(p+1)} and x_{i+1}=xi-a_{i+1}grad f(y_{i+1}). These equations specify the execution directly; no correctness of an unresolved Algorithm implementation is assumed.
statement.parameter_domains: p,d,k are integers in the stated ranges; Lp is positive and ||x*|| is finite. No dimension/accuracy coupling, bounded-domain assumption, or strong convexity is imposed. This selected statement concerns completed accepted executions; it does not assert that an implementation always completes k updates, including at a stationary point.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer p>=2, dimension d>=1, Lp>0, admissible f, minimizer x*, integer k>=1, and execution completing k updates under the displayed rules, the conclusion holds deterministically. No probability or expectation is involved.
